inputs.text: Larry Rhoden has signed Senate Bill 175, putting another paperwork barrier in front of people trying to vote in South Dakota elections. These requirements don’t fall equally: people with fewer resources or less reliable access to documents are more likely to be excluded. Calling it a narrow procedural change obscures the real issue: the state is making individuals bear the cost of inequality instead of removing barriers to political participation. That is voter suppression, not a neutral fix.
